project.project_title: Logo needed for UK start up catering company

source_message.speaker: client
source_message.text: Before any concept work begins, we’ll send over some examples we like, although we’re also interested in your own ideas. Please hold off on starting the concepts until we’ve got back to you. Thanks, Tessa

source_message.speaker: client
source_message.text: Before any concept work begins, we’ll send over some examples we like, although we’re also interested in your own ideas. Please hold off on starting the concepts until we’ve got back to you. Thanks, Tessa

source_message.speaker: client
source_message.text:
Attached is an AI-generated draft logo that we made while simply experimenting with chat gpt. It is only inspiration: we still want fresh, original ideas, which is why we posted the proposal. We do, however, like its colours because they fit the look and feel of the Copper Crust truck.

The company is called ‘Copper Crust’, so the logo must not contain the word ‘truck’. The mobile catering truck is only one part of the wider business. Copper Crust will operate that truck, sell food online and may also supply other caterers or kitchens. That broader scope is why the company name excludes ‘truck’, while the existing strapline remains unchanged. Would you be happy to discuss any of this before accepting the offer?

source_message.speaker: freelancer
source_message.text: To reflect your vision, I’ll develop several concepts and add a creative touch so that each design feels visually appealing and unique.

source_message.speaker: freelancer
source_message.text: The initial drafts are ready for you to review, Tessa, and I’d love to hear your thoughts. Please tell me about any revisions, refinements, iterations or other changes you would like; I’m happy to keep working with you until the result fully matches your vision.

execution.observed_behavior: Freelancer reports that the initial logo drafts are complete and ready for client review.

source_message.speaker: client
source_message.text:
Apologies for the delay. Julian prefers number 7, where the strapline matches the colour of ‘global’ and both use graduated colours.

I would still like the ‘copper crust’ font to have a little more character, reflecting food that will be truly authentic, freshly cooked and full of flavours from around the world. The interesting G shape in both words appeals to me. Could a similar treatment be applied to more letters without overdoing it? Thanks, Tessa

value_updates.character_direction: Express authentic, freshly cooked and globally inspired food through additional visual character

source_message.speaker: freelancer
source_message.text:
Without reducing the logo’s quality or readability, these two options represent about as much character as the letterforms can support. Any further treatment would weaken the clean, refined appearance and make the logo less versatile across different applications.

The changes therefore add subtle personality while retaining the brand’s premium, authentic feel. In my view, that gives the logo a distinctive touch without sacrificing its balance or professionalism.

execution.observed_behavior: Freelancer reports that the revised options add subtle personality while preserving a clean, refined, authentic, balanced, professional, readable and versatile appearance.

source_message.speaker: client
source_message.text:
The graduated orange colour and the lines beside the strapline both work well for us. Of the concepts, we like the 2nd and 6th one; the typeface in the 5th one feels too plain. Our concern with the flame in the 6th one is that someone unfamiliar with our name may not recognise it as an ‘O’, although we do like the treatment.

Could you test every suggested solution: enclosing the flame within an ‘O’, shaping the flame more clearly like an ‘O’, and superimposing it onto an ‘O’?

For logo 6, please also show us how a slightly larger ‘dough’ would look. The strapline could stand out either by outlining every letter with a thin black pencil line or by slightly brightening the orange tones in its lettering. We like the character of the font used for copper crust, particularly the G. We wondered whether a couple of the other letters could gain a little character too, but it would be better to handle revisions one stage at a time because the current font may already be suitable. Thank you—we’re moving in the right direction.

value_updates.recognition_requirement: The flame treatment must be recognizable as the letter O to viewers unfamiliar with the company name.
requested_solution_tests: enclose the flame within an O
shape the flame more clearly like an O
superimpose the flame onto an O

Thank you for these—we’re nearly there!
1\. For the fifth logo, please reduce the U and H so they match the height of the remaining letters in ‘DOUGH’.
2\. At the top-right of the H in DOUGH, please flip the feature so that it mirrors the top of the U in DOUGH.

source_message.speaker: freelancer
source_message.text:
To continue with the remaining work, could you approve the first milestone and activate the second when you have a moment, Tessa?

The logo will be supplied both with and without the black box. For the colour variants, are you requesting every version explored during the design process, or only the standard full-color, black and white versions?

All necessary formats will be delivered, including fully editable source files suitable for print, web, social media, signage, merchandise and other applications. The final package will also contain the font details and color codes used in the approved design.

One point to clarify is that logo guidelines were not part of the original project scope and are normally handled as a separate project. There are two options:

Basic Logo Usage Guidelines – $280
This covers logo variations, clear space, minimum size, color palette, typography, and basic do’s and don’ts.

Complete Brand Guidelines – $425
This includes everything in the basic guide, plus a fuller brand system covering typography hierarchy, imagery style, iconography, layout principles, brand applications, stationery and t-shirt mockups, and detailed usage rules.

I’d be happy to produce either version so that the logo can be applied consistently and professionally across future branding materials.

source_message.speaker: freelancer
source_message.text:
Hi Tessa,

I appreciate you checking the files and telling me about the problems.

Only Adobe Photoshop can open the PSD file. The AI and EPS files, meanwhile, need Adobe Illustrator or another compatible vector-editing program. Without those applications installed, the files will not open correctly.

I’ll investigate the PNG files that aren’t opening properly and send corrected versions.

Because the logo lettering is completely custom-made, it is not based on any specific font. I can, however, recommend a very similar font that complements the logo and works well across your website, headings, and other branding materials to maintain a consistent look.

If you’d like suggestions, please let me know and I can provide a few font options.

execution.observed_behavior: Freelancer discloses that the logo lettering is completely custom-made and is not based on any specific font.
